Si amas, ne accusa deformitatem amatoris, non
enim potest non cæcutire amans anima. Nam per-

amas, quid fles, & ingemiscis, & molestiam infers

page.notes: Left edge fragments ("ind", "ni", and similar) are neighbouring-page edge, not transcribed. The small mark before "Amat," and the initial mark before "Eth." are ornaments or stray marks, read as "Amat," and "Eth." The page ends mid-word with "la-", which continues on the next page. Spelling was normalised for long s (s) and u/v, i/j; the original printed forms "fi", "exiftentem", "poteft" and "fufficiendo" are rendered as si, existentem, potest and sufficiendo. "Ruft." is read as "Rust.", and "namq;" and "atq;" are kept as printed.
